chapter: First bands, Ennis, Thornhill and the Army
title: Marriage to singer Lilian Grace, 1950-61
summary: Gil says he was married ten or eleven years to Lilian Grace, a singer he met through Claude Thornhill's orchestra.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Were you any more financially successful when you were married to
She was like an Andrews sister though, so that might have helped. When I saw her I felt, wow, she looks like Patty Andrews, I remember. All done up (broad center?).
She had been a singer, yes. She was from Philadelphia.
And how long were you married?
Eleven I think. '50 to '60 from '50 to '61.
Was that an instant romance too?
No. No it wasn't. She was married to a saxophone player in Claude Thornhill's
orchestra and I worked with Claude Thornhill and I met her when I was playing and I with [him]

Oh, so you met her first when you were both connected with the orchestra in some way? But you had nothing to do with the fact that she was no longer married to the saxophone player I take it? (LAUGHTER).
